title: The Fit the Outliers Pulled: Fitting a Line to Points With a Few Wrong Ones, and Lines That Go Straight Up

questions.question: A robot fits y = m x + k to the points of a wall that runs straight ahead of it. What happens?
options: A vertical line has no slope, so the sums divide by zero and there is no answer; the form a x + b y + c = 0 can describe it
questions.explanation: Points on x = 3 gave a valid line at 90.0 degrees from fit_line, and no answer from the vertical distance fit.

questions.question: Why is a x + b y + c useful when a and b are a unit vector?
options: It is the signed distance from the line to the point (x, y), which is what a fit should make small

questions.question: A line has an angle of 179 degrees in one description and 1 in another. How far apart are they?
options: 2: a line has no direction, so the angle is taken modulo 180 and compared the smaller way round
questions.explanation: The suite checked that 179 and 1 are 2 degrees apart.

questions.question: 100 points on a line and 30 wrong ones in a cluster. What was the mean error of the angle fitting everything, and with the random-sample fit?
questions.explanation: A least squares fit is pulled by a far point more than by a near one.

questions.question: How does the random-sample fit choose its line?
options: It tries many lines through two random points, keeps the one most points are within the threshold of, and refits all those points
questions.explanation: The final answer uses everything that agreed, not just the two that chose it.

questions.question: When can the random-sample fit fail?
options: When more than about half the points are wrong, or the threshold does not suit the sensor's noise
questions.explanation: A threshold too large keeps the chair.
